evals.name: resolves-topic-docs-state-and-interviews-before-writing
evals.expected_output: Reads the current state in ladder order — an existing .claude/topic-docs.yaml, a working-docs convention declared in CLAUDE.md/.claude/rules, an inferred conforming layout — and reports what it found. When nothing is configured, it presents the one load-bearing decision, contract_tier, with branch marked RECOMMENDED and presented first (local as the solo/offline alternative), keeps contract_dir and memory_dir at the documented defaults (docs/topics and .work) unless the repo declares otherwise, and writes nothing until the user accepts.
expectations: Reads .claude/topic-docs.yaml first, then a declared working-docs convention, then an inferred conforming layout — in that order
Presents the single contract_tier decision with branch as the RECOMMENDED first option and invents no further knobs
Keeps contract_dir and memory_dir at the documented defaults unless the repo's own conventions say otherwise
Writes nothing until the user accepts the values

evals.name: rerun-preserves-existing-concern-file-keys
evals.prompt:
/planning:setup

This repo already has a .claude/topic-docs.yaml containing memory_dir: .scratch and vault_backend: gitbook.
evals.expected_output: Reports the existing concern file's effective values as the baseline (memory_dir: .scratch, vault_backend: gitbook, other keys at the documented defaults) and proposes changes against it rather than overwriting blind. It explicitly reports that GitBook is deferred and non-writable, so durable writes still use docs and no GitBook API, MCP, or Git Sync writer is configured. Whatever the user changes, the re-run preserves every key the existing file carries — it never drops memory_dir or vault_backend — and writes nothing until the user accepts.
expectations: Reports the existing file's effective values (absent keys = documented defaults) as the interview baseline
Reports vault_backend: gitbook as preserved but deferred and non-writable, with docs as the effective promotion target
Does not configure, test, or invoke a GitBook API, MCP, or Git Sync writer
Preserves every key the existing concern file carries — a re-run never drops one
Does not invent knobs beyond the schema
Writes nothing until the user accepts the values

evals.name: conflict-check-and-write-guards
evals.prompt:
/planning:setup

Use the defaults; this repo's .gitignore contains a docs/ ignore rule.
evals.expected_output: Before writing, runs git check-ignore -v on the chosen contract root and, because an ignore rule matches docs/topics, stops and surfaces the exact rule and its source line rather than silently producing an uncommittable contract tier. It never edits the consumer's root .gitignore (resolving the rule is the user's edit), writes only the tracked .claude/topic-docs.yaml once the conflict is cleared — recording only non-default keys — and never writes the plugin directory or the plugin data directory.
expectations: Runs git check-ignore -v on the contract root before writing and surfaces the exact matching rule and source
Never edits the consumer's root .gitignore or any ignore file
Persists to the tracked .claude/topic-docs.yaml, recording only the keys the user chose
Does not write the plugin directory or the plugin data directory

evals.name: standards-bootstrap-second-run-is-a-no-op
evals.prompt:
/planning:setup

Set up the standards concern. This repo already has docs/standards/README.md with standards-contract frontmatter at the binding's current version, valid row paths, and a docs/standards/.gitignore containing *.local.md from a previous run of this setup.
evals.expected_output: The standards bootstrap reads state in order (concern file, then the index presence test, then inference sources), finds a conforming index at the binding's contract version, validates the row paths, and short-circuits: it reports the index healthy and proposes no changes — a second run produces no diff. It does not re-interview, does not rewrite the index or the setup-owned overlay .gitignore, does not offer a migration (versions match), and touches no other ignore file.
expectations: Reads state via the binding's procedure: concern file, index presence test, then inference sources
Recognizes the conforming current-version index and proposes no changes (second run yields no diff)
Does not re-run the interview when the index is healthy at the binding's version
Does not offer migration when the index version matches the binding
Edits no ignore file other than the setup-owned standards-root .gitignore, and here leaves even that untouched
